sections.h2: What should a seller know about Pierce County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat. According to the county, the land came from Appling and Ware counties when Pierce was organized in 1857, and the name honors President Franklin Pierce. The Alabaha River winds through it, and its website points visitors toward fishing and the history of the Okefenokee.

It is the most spread-out county in the four-county Census comparison. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 count is 20,764 people, up 5.3 percent on 2020, over 340.46 square miles of land. That works out to 57.9 people per square mile in 2020. The county issued only 68 building permits in 2025, the fewest of the four compared, so a resale competes with little new housing.

Prices reflect that. The median owner-occupied value is $153,300 in the 2020 to 2024 estimates. Roughly three homes in four (76.5 percent) are owner-occupied, and rent is a median $799. Median household income was $60,517, and 82.9 percent of households have broadband. With prices like these, unpaid tax can swallow a large part of the proceeds, so learn the balance early.

Storm damage can also affect a sale. The county's home page carries a notice that Hurricane Debby damaged personal and business property and that the emergency management agency collected damage reports from residents and business owners for a federal disaster relief application. A seller with a damaged roof or outbuilding should keep photographs and repair estimates, since a buyer's inspection will ask about them.

sections.h2: Which Pierce County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Duties divide between the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, whose addresses are both on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's page describes an office independent of the assessors and of the county commissioners, who control only its budget. The commissioner's main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

Pierce County tax offices, from the county and commissioner websites

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and the site says online payments post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 Pierce County millage notice say?
sections.html:
A notice on the county's millage page says commissioners tentatively set a 2025 rate that raises property tax by 19.98 percent in unincorporated areas and 20.20 percent in incorporated ones. The hearings were held at the NFC Building at 705 College Avenue in Blackshear on November 6 and November 13, 2025, and those dates have passed.

  • Tentative millage rate: 11.241 mills.
  • Increase over the prior rate: 1.872 mills.
  • Rate without the increase: no more than 9.369 mills.
  • Increase printed for unincorporated areas: 19.98 percent; for incorporated areas: 20.20 percent.

That page also links the 2025 digest with its five-year levy history, plus the prior year's digest. Three authorities set millage: the commissioners, the school board and the State. A tentative rate may change before it is final, so ask the commissioner which millage is on your bill and whether the parcel lies in Blackshear, Patterson or unincorporated land.

sections.h2: When is Pierce County property tax due?
sections.html:
Your bill carries the due date, and the commissioner's office can confirm it by phone. The state revenue department's county facts page explains the range. December 20 is the official date, yet a county can pass a resolution for December 1 or November 15, or can split billing into installments.

State rules give you some breathing room, and a few other facts help sellers:

  • Per the state's county facts page, interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can follow if the balance goes delinquent.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • The return window at the county tax office runs January 1 to April 1.
  • A manufactured home parked in Pierce on January 1 gets its return and its location permit on the same visit, before April 1.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Pierce County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. The assessor's FAQ says late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If the value stands, the Pierce County Grand Jury's appointees on the three-person Board of Equalization hear the dispute next.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers work from three methods (cost, comparable sales and income). Field staff may stop at a parcel to look into an appeal, a return, a new addition or a conservation application. Visitors from the office show photo identification and arrive in a marked county vehicle. To meet with the Board of Assessors, book by the Friday before its 9:00 a.m. session; the board sits at least twice monthly.

sections.h2: What exemptions and special assessments apply in Pierce County?
sections.html:
The Pierce County homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. A purchase made after New Year's Day misses that year's exemption, since the January 1 test looks at who owned and lived there. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The Georgia Department of Revenue's county page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so state exemptions are what applies; ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

The assessor's FAQ lists special programs that can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential farmland is assessed at 30 percent instead of 40, and the owner commits to ten years of farm use.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Trees on the stump escape tax until they are sold or cut, then count at full market value.

Land held under a covenant deserves a question to the assessors, before the contract is signed, about how a sale or a new use changes things. The county has 57.9 people per square mile, so farm and timber parcels are a real part of its sales, and the covenant terms are worth requesting in writing.

faqs.q: Where is the Pierce County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

faqs.q: What is the Pierce County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Ask the commissioner or check your bill. December 20 is the state's default, which a county can replace with an earlier date or installments.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: Written appeals must arrive inside 45 days of the notice date. The assessors' FAQ calls any later appeal invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

faqs.q: When must a Pierce County homestead exemption be filed?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want it. Ownership and residence on January 1 of that year are both required.
